accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Year 2 Plants statutory requirement (find out and describe how plants need water, light and a suitable temperature to grow and stay healthy) and NGSS 2-LS2-1. The outcomes are correct: no water gives wilting and browning; darkness gives tall, thin, pale (etiolated) growth that fails; cold slows growth; waterlogged roots lack air so leaves yellow and droop. The plant heights are labelled in the adult text as a model, and the lab never says the dark plant is healthy despite being taller.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years ideas: plants get their food from the soil or soil alone is enough; more water is always better; the tallest plant must be the healthiest (etiolation); plants grow anywhere regardless of temperature; and the unfair test that moves a pot into the dark and also stops its water. Each appears as a prediction option, challenge distractor or fair-test message.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagplantneed compares two pots for one week with one condition changed at a time (water, light, warmth), adds a three-level water amount, a fair-test checker that names which extra variable was changed, and a sad plant fixed by giving each missing need. flagseed models germination of a seed and flagxylem models water moving up a stem; neither varies growing conditions. Shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child chooses a condition and jumps a week before being told the rule: pot B flops brown with no water, goes pale and spindly in the cupboard and stays small in the fridge; too much water turns the leaves yellow; the fair test only unlocks the week button when the light is the one difference; and the sad plant recovers only when water, light and warmth have all been given.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 'grow bigger' without water, 'grow better' in the dark, 'grow the fastest' in the fridge, 'yes, always' more water, 'the light and the water' for a fair test, and 'just a bigger pot' for the sad plant. The week-later pictures disprove each.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong answers are tagged dark, same, cold, flood, fair, silly or soil, each with its own one-line correction: no light means no food so pale and weak, plants change when they miss a need, cold means hardly any growth, too much water drowns roots, change only one thing, and soil alone is not enough.

readability.evidence: Kid text Flesch-Kincaid grade 0.2 (family target ≤ 5), key idea 1.6: very short sentences and everyday words (dry, flop, pale, fridge, puddle) for ages 6 to 8. Adult text grade 5.3 names etiolation and waterlogging plainly.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any lesson. Kid paragraphs: the three needs, water and light, warmth, too much water. Adult paragraphs: curriculum placement, biology and model caveat, named mistakes, what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in both themes: two pots, their labels and the one-week result words fit the 390 px canvas; buttons use a 52 px minimum height and 1.06 rem text for young children and wrap without clipping; the dark cupboard and fridge panels sit behind the plant without covering labels.

accessibility.evidence: Every tap on the canvas has a big labelled button (Water pot A, No water for pot B, B by the window / in the cupboard, Warm room / Fridge, No water / Some water / Too much, the three fair-test toggles and Is it fair?, Water / Light / Warmth, One week later / Day 1) with aria-pressed where it is a choice. The canvas aria-label reports each pot's result after every week. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
